summary: Frontend-only regression for the expired/revoked session fix. All 8 specified scenarios passed end-to-end against the public preview URL. The 401 axios interceptor clears the query cache, resets user state, shows the 'Your session has expired. Please sign in again.' sonner toast (visible in bottom-right), and Guard redirects to /login without ever showing ErrorState or getting stuck on Loading. ErrorState correctly renders the server-provided message (QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE -> 'Maintenance could not be queued.') for a 503, and falls back to 'HTTP 500' text for a body-less 500 while keeping the user logged in. Retry works, invalid-password inline error still shows without the expired toast, sidebar logout works, deep links redirect to /login, and desktop + mobile 390x844 layouts have no horizontal overflow.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthProvider.tsx guards toast with userRef.current so a background /auth/me 401 on first load does not spam the toast — good; but the interceptor is registered inside a useEffect that depends on queries, meaning during the first render (before the effect runs) any 401 slips through without cleanup. Low risk since only /auth/me runs before mount, but consider registering the interceptor at module scope or with useLayoutEffect for defense in depth.

index.js retry policy: `(!error?.response || error.response.status >= 500) && failureCount < 2` retries on network errors (no response), which is desirable, but note this still allows retries on 5xx which may extend user wait; consider surfacing loading feedback for retried queries.
